data.description:
# Evaluate whether the munitoai-free rate-limit budget is effective

discovered-from:LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want an evidence-based answer to *"is the
`rate_limit_rpm: 10` budget on the `munitoai-free` tier actually doing its job?"*
— measured from real proxy logs over the first ~12 hours after the budget went
live — so I can keep it, raise it, lower it, or replace it with header-derived
budgeting (`LP-0MVDNP36J006430L`) instead of guessing.

## Context

`LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` shipped in commit `b71d743a` and the proxy was restarted
with it at **2026-10-18 13:59:31 local (BST)**. Live behaviour as designed:

- entries with `rate_limit_rpm` accept at most N dispatches per rolling 60-second
  window (`munitoai-free` is configured with `rate_limit_rpm: 10` on the `plan`,
  `author` and `code` chains — one shared bucket per provider entry name);
- an over-budget request from a **new** session (no affinity) skips the entry
  immediately and the chain continues — it never waits;
- an over-budget request from a session already served by the entry waits (up to
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds`, default 60) for the window to
  drain, then dispatches on the free tier;
- affinity is TTL-scoped (`server.provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`, default 900);
- remaining budget is displayed in the provider diagnostics table on `/`
  (`budget N/10 per 60s`).

The starting value of 10 was a judgement call: the observed peak before the gate
was **41 dispatches per rolling minute** (2026-10-18 11:27) with upstream
`HTTP 429 rate_limit_exceeded` responses at peaks.

## Evaluation method (run against `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`)

Window A (post-change): from the restart marker at `2026-10-18 13:59:31` to the
evaluation time. Window B (baseline, pre-change): the equivalent preceding span
(e.g. 12 h ending 13:59:31) from the same plus rotated logs.

1. **Dispatch rate vs budget** — for every `[remote] POST … ->
   https://api.munito.ai/inference` line, compute the maximum number of
   dispatches in any rolling 60 s window, plus the per-minute distribution
   (median/p95/max) and the count of windows at/over 10. Expect: rolling max
   ≤ 10 (plus in-flight retries of the same logical request, which are not
   separately budgeted).
2. **Skips** — count `Provider budget exhausted:` lines; break down by
   `reason=` (`rate_limited`, `rate_limited_waiters`, `rate_limited_after_wait`,
   `rate_limited_disconnect`) and by `session_affinity=`; confirm every
   `session_affinity=false` skip was followed by a dispatch to the next tier and
   that no wait occurred for it.
3. **Waits** — count `Provider budget wait start|satisfied|exhausted|aborted`
   lines and the distribution of `waited=` values (target ≤ 60 s; flag any wait
   that consumed a large share of a client's latency).
4. **Upstream 429s** — count MunitoAI `429` / `rate_limit_exceeded` occurrences
   in window A vs window B, both absolute and as a share of MunitoAI dispatches.
   Expect a material reduction.
5. **Free-tier utilisation preserved** — share of minutes where the free tier was
   used at all, and mean dispatches per active minute. A budget that is never
   reached means the free tier is under-used (wasted headroom); a budget that is
   always saturated at peak means pressure simply moved to paid tiers.
6. **Regression check** — confirm there is no increase in `All providers
   exhausted` / terminal 503s, and no visible increase in first-token latency on
   the free tier caused by waiting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A reproducible analysis (script or documented commands) is run over the two
   windows and its raw output is attached to this work item as a comment.
2. Measured rolling-60s max dispatches to `munitoai-free` in the post-change
   window is reported against the configured budget of 10, with a verdict on
   whether the gate holds.
3. The skip/waits breakdown (reasons, `session_affinity` split, waited-duration
   distribution) is reported, including explicit confirmation that new-session
   skips did **not** wait and that in-progress waits stayed within the cap.
4. Upstream MunitoAI `429`/`rate_limit_exceeded` rate is compared across the two
   windows (absolute + share of dispatches) and the change is quantified.
5. Free-tier utilisation is reported (share of minutes used, dispatches per
   active minute) with an assessment of over- vs under-restriction.
6. A concrete recommendation is recorded — keep `rate_limit_rpm: 10`, raise it,
   lower it, or hand the value to header-derived budgeting
   (`LP-0MVDNP36J006430L`) — with the evidence that supports it, plus any change
   to `provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds` / `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`.
7. If the recommendation changes configuration or code, the change is implemented
   with tests and `proxy/config.yaml` / `proxy/config-fast.yaml` +
   `proxy/README.md` updated; the full project test suite must pass.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect any findings that change
   documented behaviour (code comments, `README`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`).

## Constraints

- Read-only on production state: do not restart the proxy, edit config, or
  change limits as part of the *measurement* (only as a follow-up change per
  AC7, in its own worktree).
- Use the test skill for any test execution; do not run ad-hoc test commands.
- Treat missing log fields as absent, not zero, and state the log window
  boundaries used (rotation can leave gaps).
- Keep the free tier in the chain: the goal is right-sizing, not removal.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` (completed, in_review) — the budget gate this evaluates.
- `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` (open) — header-derived (`x-ratelimit-*`) budgeting/reset,
  the likely successor for the static value.
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` (open) — restrict the free tier to cheap mode only.
- `LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N` (completed) — per-account 429 must not exclude the paid
  MunitoAI sibling.

## Scheduled dispatch

This item is dispatched automatically **12 hours after the budget went live**
(one-shot cron, 2026-10-19 02:05 local) so a full post-change window exists.
The kickoff script self-removes its cron entry after firing.

data.description:
# Give the model (fallback chain) config control over the free-tier request budget

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want to set the free-tier request-budget behaviour
**per model / fallback chain** (with sensible global defaults), so I can tune
`plan`, `author`, `code` and `compact` independently — instead of every model
inheriting one global setting — while any single provider entry can still
override its own behaviour.

## Current state

- `rate_limit_rpm` is a **provider-entry** field (`provider_cfg`), so it is
  already configurable per entry — today only `munitoai-free` sets it (10).
- The four *behaviour* knobs are read **server-wide only**:
  `server.provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio`,
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds`,
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_waiters`,
  `server.provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py::_config_value`, called with the server
  config).
- `acquire_provider_budget(provider_cfg, config, session_id, request)` is **not**
  given `model_config`/the model name, so a model-scoped setting cannot be
  expressed today — a single reserve ratio / wait cap applies to all chains.
- Consequence: an interactive chain (e.g. `plan`) and a background chain (e.g.
  `compact`) cannot trade latency against free-tier utilisation differently, and
  a future gated entry cannot be tuned without changing global behaviour.

## Desired change

Add a **model-level `budget` block** with precedence
**provider entry > model block > server default > built-in default**:

```yaml
models:
  plan:
    budget:
      reserve_ratio: 0.4        # share of rate_limit_rpm reserved for in-progress
      wait_max_seconds: 10      # per-request wait cap for in-progress sessions
      max_waiters: 4            # concurrent waiter cap
      affinity_ttl_seconds: 600 # how long a session counts as in-progress
    providers:
      - name: munitoai-free
        rate_limit_rpm: 15      # entry-level override of the budget size
        budget:                 # optional per-entry behaviour override
          reserve_ratio: 0.2
```

- All five keys are optional at every layer; absent keys fall through to the next
  layer, so **existing configs behave exactly as today**.
- Values are clamped/validated exactly as the server-level knobs are today
  (ratio to `[0,1]`, wait/TTL to `>= 0`, malformed values fall back to the
  default with a warning — fail open, never fail closed).
- The effective values are visible per request in the budget logs/attempt
  diagnostics (which layer supplied `reserve_slots`/`effective_limit`), and the
  provider diagnostics table keeps showing remaining/limit per entry.
- The budget **bucket** remains keyed by provider entry (one account quota shared
  by `plan`/`author`/`code` even when their model blocks differ) — document this
  explicitly so per-model tuning is not mistaken for per-model quota.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `models.<name>.budget` block is honoured for `reserve_ratio`,
   `wait_max_seconds`, `max_waiters` and `affinity_ttl_seconds`, and a provider
   entry may override any of them with its own `budget` block.
2. Precedence is exactly entry > model > server > built-in default, proven by
   tests for every key (single-layer and multi-layer combinations).
3. Omitting all blocks reproduces today's behaviour byte-for-byte (no behavioural
   change; tested).
4. Malformed/out-of-range values fall back to the next layer with a logged
   warning and never raise or block a request (tests for each key).
5. The budget bucket stays shared per provider entry across models; a test proves
   two models with different `budget` blocks still consume one `rate_limit_rpm`
   window.
6. The effective configuration is visible in the budget skip/wait log lines and
   the attempt diagnostics (source layer included), and the provider diagnostics
   table keeps showing remaining/limit.
7. Tests cover both fallback entry points (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`,
  `_proxy_with_fallback`) and the compaction/summarizer path where it reaches the
  same gate.
8. Documentation updated: `proxy/config.yaml` header comments + a commented
   example, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`
   (model-level `budget` block alongside the `providers` list).
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Config-shape only: no change to gate semantics, reserve maths, or the
  affinity/wait design.
- Keep every layer optional; no migration of existing configs required.
- Do not introduce per-model *quota* (a separate budget per model) — that would
  break the one-account-per-entry model; if it is ever wanted, it must be a
  separate decision.
- The gate must remain fail-open when the new blocks are absent or malformed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — resolve each knob through the new
  entry > model > server precedence; extend `BudgetDecision`/logs with the source
  layer.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — pass `model_config` (and the model key) into
  `acquire_provider_budget()` from both fallback entry points.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — document the `models.<name>.budget` block; commented
  example.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` — precedence/validation/shared-bucket
  tests.
- `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` + fixtures — only if the new keys are
  introduced as shipped values (they are optional; likely no fixture change).
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` — docs.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — reserve + 15 s wait cap (introduced the knobs this item
  makes per-model).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` — the original budget gate.
- `LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4` — evaluating whether the `munitoai-free` budget itself
  should be raised (the first consumer of per-model tuning).
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` — restricting the free tier to cheap mode (another
  model-scoped policy that could share this configuration shape).

data.comment:
## Producer decision (2026-10-18): accepted — Option A

Producer accepted the rotation-limited evidence as sufficient for the sizing
decision (option A of the review findings).

- **Verdict recorded:** the 40,960 MiB cap is not harming the workload; no
  further raise is warranted (`--recommend` outputs 27,648 MiB this run and
  39,936 MiB from the 1,065-request interim are both <= 40,960 MiB).
- **Directional confirmation:** eviction rate ~halved per request
  (1.28%/req at 32,768 MiB -> 0.94%/req at 40,960 MiB, both captured under
  load) and 0 evictions / 0% saturation in the lower-load surviving fragment.
- **Explicitly not proven (accepted limitation):** "evictions ~0 under
  sustained load" — the cap still saturated at 99.8% with 10 evictions in the
  1,065-request interim; a full-window retest is impossible because the
  llama-server numbered logs rotated away (LP-0MVE0JS3B005PWY2 tracks the
  retention fix so future windows remain reconstructible).
- AC1 and AC5 met; AC2–AC4 accepted as documented (rotation-limited + 
  restart-confounded) rather than blocking.

Closing with this decision recorded.
